narrative_summary: SPX closed at 7,533.77, slipping back off the 6/15 swing high (7,577.92) on yet another failed test while holding above the 23.6% fib (7,498) and the ERP floor. The bull skeleton is mechanically intact — 50-day above a rising 200-day, price ~7.9% over the 200-day and above the 20/50-day — but late-cycle confirmation risk dominates: ERP has fallen to ~0.0% (a valuation ceiling), McClellan breadth remains near its lows, credit is only neutral, and the Monte Carlo edge has cooled to 63.4% up-first, failing all regime thresholds. Posture stays trim-biased: patience at resistance, no aggressive adds, with defined re-entry structure lower.
